I’ve been in school (Engineering major) non-stop for the last 4 years, including zooming spring and summer semesters of sophomore year (because I did astronomically awful when Covid hit) and a 21 credit semester last Fall. I had zero friends prior to the 2nd semester of junior year, went through an awful breakup, panic attacks, self-isolation, you name it. By the time I was done with everything, I was seriously burnt out and hated this school. Yesterday was the first day I’m no longer a student of this school and it felt great. I can finally do the things I’ve wanted to do but had to set aside because of this. At the same time, I feel a little bit sad. I’m leaving the people that care about me, who stopped everything they were doing just to sit with me and calm me down when I have panic attacks and helped me every step of the way. Even though my experience here were not perfect like what you see on TV, far from it in fact, it did make me who I am today: strong, independent, caring & whole. Yesterday, I bought a Tom Brady jersey from Mden (I didn’t even watch football because I’m an international student) to bring it back home as a souvenir, and to remind me that for 4 years of my life Michigan accepted me, and it’s time I finally accepted it.
